entry.content:
Hardware competition and geopolitics dominated the infrastructure story:

  • Etched hit a $5B valuation with $1B in booked contracts for its specialized inference chip.
  • Taiwanese authorities raided Super Micro offices in a probe over alleged Nvidia chip smuggling to China.

On AI-for-science and safety, Meta AI unveiled Brain2Qwerty v2, a non-invasive MEG brain-to-text pipeline reaching 61% word accuracy, and OpenAI launched the GeneBench-Pro genomics benchmark. A new labor report found high-intensity AI adopters grew headcount 10.2%, countering job-loss fears, while researchers disclosed a new jailbreak exposing risks in agentic AI browsers.

entry.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 as a cheaper way to run agents
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5, its most agentic mid-tier model, delivering stronger agentic capabilities, lower pricing, and improved safety. It is positioned as a cheaper alternative to Opus, GPT-5.5, and Gemini Pro for running agents.

entry.title: Meta AI Releases Brain2Qwerty v2: A Non-Invasive MEG Brain-to-Text Pipeline Decoding Typed Sentences at 61% Word Accuracy
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Reddit discussion, today's coverage supplies the concrete accuracy figures and the code release, Meta AI released Brain2Qwerty v2, a non-invasive MEG brain-to-text pipeline decoding typed sentences in real time at 61% average word accuracy, up from 8% for prior non-invasive methods, with the best participant reaching 78%. Meta also released full training code for both versions.

entry.title: Nvidia competitor Etched hits $5B valuation, $1B in sales for AI chip
entry.summary: Nvidia chip challenger Etched reached a $5B valuation and says it has booked $1B in contracts for inference systems powered by its specialized chip. It represents growing momentum for dedicated inference silicon competing with Nvidia.

entry.title: Google's new Nano Banana 2 Lite image model is its fastest and cheapest yet
entry.summary: Google DeepMind released Nano Banana 2 Lite, technically Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image, its fastest and cheapest image model, available across the Google ecosystem. It targets rapid prototyping while claiming quality close to Google's heavier image models.

entry.title: Meituan's LongCat-2.0 shows China can train massive AI models without Nvidia
entry.summary: First surfaced on Reddit as the stealth 'owl-alpha' model — today's coverage develops the geopolitical angle of an entirely Nvidia-free, all-Chinese training run, Meituan reportedly trained LongCat-2.0, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model, entirely on Chinese chips without any Nvidia hardware. It demonstrates China's growing ability to train massive models on domestic silicon amid export restrictions.

entry.title: Anthropic's new Claude Sonnet 5 closes the gap to Opus model series
entry.summary: The Decoder details Claude Sonnet 5, which beats predecessor Sonnet 4.6 on all benchmarks and edges out the larger Opus 4.8 on the GDPval-AA v2 knowledge-work test at 1,618. Anthropic emphasized the model's deliberately low cybersecurity capability, a likely signal amid export-control debates.

entry.title: The Trump Administration Is Lifting Its Export Controls on Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable AI Models
entry.summary: The White House is reportedly easing export restrictions on Anthropic's most advanced Mythos and Fable models, weeks after ordering the company to suspend foreign-national access. The reversal signals volatility in US policy governing frontier model access abroad.

entry.title: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 vs Sonnet 4.6 vs Opus 4.8: Agentic Coding Benchmarks, API Pricing, and Cost-Performance Tradeoffs Compared
entry.summary: A detailed comparison shows Claude Sonnet 5 beating Sonnet 4.6 on every benchmark (63.2% SWE-bench Pro, 81.2% OSWorld-Verified, 57.4% HLE) at $2/$10 intro pricing versus Opus 4.8's $5/$25. It notes Sonnet 5 offers best value at low/medium effort but can exceed Opus cost at extra-high effort, with deliberately low cyber capability.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Claude Science bets on workflow, not a new model, to win over scientists
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Science, a workbench giving researchers a unified environment for computational research across databases, pipelines, and tools. The bet is on workflow integration rather than a new model to win over scientists.

entry.title: Meta secretly tested ChatGPT, Gemini, and Character.AI with thousands of minor-perspective crisis prompts
entry.summary: Meta reportedly had hundreds of contractors pose as minors and send tens of thousands of suicide, sex, and drug-related crisis prompts to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Character.AI without the companies' knowledge. A single round involved over 45,000 prompts, raising ethics and competitive-testing questions.

entry.title: Claude Science is Anthropic’s newest flagship product
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on Claude Science, Anthropic's new flagship product supporting scientific research the way Claude Code supports engineering, now available to all paid subscribers. Anthropic will also use it internally to research drugs for rare neglected diseases.

entry.title: OpenAI reportedly cut response costs for guest ChatGPT users by more than half
entry.summary: According to The Information, OpenAI cut inference costs for its models by more than half, at times dropping the number of Nvidia GPUs needed to serve ChatGPT to just a few hundred. It highlights dramatic efficiency gains in serving frontier models at scale.

entry.title: Start building with Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash
entry.summary: Google DeepMind published a builder-focused announcement for Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash, its new fast image model and API-accessible video generation model. It encourages developers to start building with both.

entry.title: Google introduces a faster, cheaper image generator with Nano Banana 2 Lite
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers Google's Nano Banana 2 Lite release, a faster and cheaper image generator aimed at creators making AI content. It reiterates the model's positioning as a lower-cost option in Google's lineup.

entry.title: Anthropic launches Claude Science, an AI workspace built specifically for researchers
entry.summary: The Decoder covers Claude Science's launch, noting over 60 preconfigured skills across genomics and computational chemistry, a verification agent that checks citations and calculations, and local or HPC-cluster deployment so sensitive data stays in-lab. It targets research workflows with privacy in mind.

entry.title: The AI jobs debate just got messier
entry.summary: A new report finds high-intensity AI adopters saw headcount rise 10.2%, with entry-level roles up 12%, countering claims that AI destroys junior jobs. The data complicates the prevailing narrative on AI and employment.

entry.title: Taiwan raids Super Micro offices in probe over Nvidia chip smuggling to China
entry.summary: Taiwanese authorities raided the offices of Super Micro Computer and several local partners as part of a probe into alleged Nvidia chip smuggling to China. It signals intensifying enforcement of chip export controls.

entry.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5 on AWS: Anthropic’s most capable Sonnet model
entry.summary: AWS announced Claude Sonnet 5 availability on Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS, offering top-tier intelligence at Sonnet pricing with enterprise security and regional data residency. It brings the new model into existing AWS environments.

entry.title: New attack provides one more reason why AI browsers are a bad idea
entry.summary: A newly disclosed attack tricks AI browsers into a manipulated context where safety guardrails no longer apply, letting them be steered into harmful actions like leaking credentials or executing sensitive tasks. The piece argues reactive guardrails treat symptoms rather than the root architectural risk of blending browsing with agentic LLM actions.

entry.title: Introducing GeneBench-Pro
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced GeneBench-Pro, a benchmark testing AI performance in genomics, biology, and scientific research using complex real-world datasets. It provides a new yardstick for evaluating models on scientific tasks.

entry.title: Frequent AI chatbot users more likely to believe anti-vaccine myths, poll finds
entry.summary: A KFF poll of 2,480 US adults found that frequent use of AI chatbots for health advice correlates with belief in vaccine myths such as autism claims, even controlling for demographics and partisanship. It raises concerns about chatbots amplifying health misinformation.

entry.title: Amazon launches new $1 billion FDE org, following OpenAI and Anthropic
entry.summary: Amazon launched a $1B forward-deployed-engineer organization whose engineers embed within customer companies to build and deploy purpose-built agents. It follows similar FDE moves by OpenAI and Anthropic.

entry.title: Rocky week for AI as shares slump but no sign of crash – yet
entry.summary: This TechScape column covers a rough week for AI stocks amid bubble fears, alongside California's proposed billionaire tax and shifting political dynamics. It surveys market sentiment souring on AI without declaring a crash.

entry.title: US campaigns now run on AI at nearly every step, and Europe is drawing a harder line
entry.summary: A New York Times report finds US Republican and Democratic campaigns now use AI at nearly every step, from opposition research to voter micro-targeting, while Europe adopts far stricter limits. It highlights a widening transatlantic divide on AI in elections.

entry.title: The DeepMind trio who built a poker AI are now making money for quant hedge funds
entry.summary: EquiLibre Technologies, a Prague lab founded by three ex-DeepMind poker-AI researchers, is now valued above $500M applying reinforcement learning to quant hedge fund trading. It marks a high-profile crossover of game-solving AI into finance.

entry.title: With Claude Science, Anthropic Targets Another Application
entry.summary: AI Business reports on Claude Science, noting Anthropic is not the first provider to target science and is proceeding cautiously given the challenges of applying AI to research. It frames the launch as another vertical application bet.

entry.title: Return of the ‘greybeards’: AI backfired – so Ford had to rehire humans
entry.summary: Ford reportedly found that hundreds of AI cameras used for design and manufacturing quality checks were unreliable, forcing the company to rehire experienced human engineers dubbed greybeards. It underscores limits of AI vision systems in high-stakes industrial workflows.

entry.title: Ahmad Osman on why local AI is catching up
entry.summary: Latent Space interviews Ahmad Osman, a longtime local-AI advocate and Osmantic founder, arguing that the gap between open-source and closed frontier models keeps shrinking. The theme resonated at the AI Engineer World's Fair as open models gain credibility.

entry.title: Vibe-coding platform Base44 launches own model as AI startups seek defensibility
entry.summary: Wix-owned vibe-coding platform Base44 began rolling out its own AI model, hoping to eventually outperform frontier models and build defensibility beyond wrapping others' models. It reflects a broader trend of app-layer startups vertically integrating into model development.

entry.title: Google launches Nano Banana 2 Lite for fast AI images and Gemini Omni Flash for video via API
entry.summary: Google launched Nano Banana 2 Lite, generating images in four seconds at $0.034 each, and Gemini Omni Flash, which brings text-prompt video generation and editing to the API for the first time. Google recommends chaining both to turn a quick image into an animated video.

entry.title: OpenClaw is finally available on Android and iOS
entry.summary: OpenClaw, a free open-source agentic program, is now available on Android and iOS, extending its autonomous agent capabilities to mobile. The launch brings open agentic tooling directly to smartphones.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Claude Models Now Available in Microsoft Foundry
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude models became available in Microsoft Foundry, giving enterprises broader access for building domain-specific autonomous agents. It expands distribution of Claude across major enterprise platforms.

entry.title: How ChatGPT adoption has expanded
entry.summary: OpenAI published Signals data showing ChatGPT adoption growing globally, with users increasing usage, exploring more capabilities, and expanding across regions and languages. It documents the platform's continued worldwide diffusion.

entry.title: Meet the lawyer who beat Elon Musk — twice
entry.summary: A profile of attorney Bill Savitt, who cross-examined Elon Musk in Musk v. Altman, recounts Musk's frustrated testimony in his lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI. The piece offers color on high-profile AI-governance litigation.

entry.title: Crypto exchange OKX wants AI agents to hire and pay each other
entry.summary: Crypto exchange OKX is building a marketplace combining payments, identity, and reputation so AI agents can hire and pay each other. It aims to bootstrap an agent-to-agent economy on crypto rails.

entry.title: X now offers an MCP server to make its platform easier for AI tools to use
entry.summary: X launched a hosted Model Context Protocol server, making it easier for developers to connect AI applications to its platform API. It reflects broader adoption of MCP as a standard for AI tool integration.

entry.title: ‘There’s this deep mystery of what, actually, is this thing?’: the philosopher inside Google DeepMind AI
entry.summary: A feature profiles Iason Gabriel, a philosopher who has worked on AI ethics at Google DeepMind since 2017, exploring whether ethicists can influence AI development amid mounting commercial and geopolitical pressure. It examines the deep uncertainty about what AI systems fundamentally are.

entry.title: Netflix is using an AI-generated Gene Wilder voice in its Willy Wonka reality show
entry.summary: Netflix is using an AI-generated Gene Wilder voice, produced via ElevenLabs with family consent, for its Willy Wonka reality show premiering in September. It continues Netflix's pattern of recreating deceased performers' voices.

entry.title: Emily Bender Sets the Record Straight on “Stochastic Parrots”
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum interviews Emily Bender, revisiting the 2021 Stochastic Parrots paper five years on and clarifying its arguments about LLMs predicting word sequences without understanding. It reflects on how the metaphor spread through AI discourse.

entry.title: Silicon Valley donations make Colorado Democratic primary one of state’s most expensive
entry.summary: Tech-executive-funded political groups, including committees led by Eric Schmidt and Chris Larsen, poured over $2M into a Colorado Democratic House primary as pro- and anti-AI factions clash over regulation. The race exemplifies AI regulation becoming a major campaign-finance battleground.

entry.title: ScarfBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Java Framework Migration
entry.summary: IBM Research introduced ScarfBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on enterprise Java framework migration tasks. It targets a practical, high-value software-modernization use case for agentic coding.

entry.title: Trump's plan to redesign every .gov website leads to AI-designed horrors
entry.summary: Trump's National Design Studio effort to use AI to rapidly overhaul 27,000 government websites is reportedly producing poor, AI-designed results, worsened by DOGE cuts to the agencies that previously maintained web standards. It highlights the pitfalls of vibe-coding critical public infrastructure on tight timelines.

entry.title: Google’s NotebookLM can sum up your research in a TikTok-style clip
entry.summary: Google's NotebookLM added TikTok-style 60-second vertical AI video overviews for Ultra and Pro subscribers, generated from uploaded sources. It extends NotebookLM's suite of AI content formats alongside podcasts and explainers.

entry.title: Acti puts AI agents directly into your smartphone keyboard
entry.summary: Startup Acti launched an AI-agent smartphone keyboard for iOS and Android that works across apps and lets users build custom natural-language shortcuts. It bets the keyboard is the next surface for embedded AI assistants.

entry.title: Libby will filter out AI content, kind of
entry.summary: Library ebook app Libby, under new OverDrive leadership, is introducing AI content controls letting readers filter AI-generated books as the publishing industry braces for a flood of such titles. The controls are partial rather than comprehensive.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: The AINews digest reports a quiet day around the AI Engineer World's Fair, highlighting Meta's non-invasive brain-to-text milestone as the top technical topic and the growing focus on building better Skills for agents. It captures conference vibes more than hard news.

entry.title: Microsoft builds a bouncer to keep bots out of Teams meetings
entry.summary: Microsoft built a feature requiring a human to verify a bot's identity in a Teams meeting lobby, aiming to stop unwanted bots from auto-joining meetings. It addresses privacy and security risks from transcription and third-party bots entering sensitive discussions.

entry.title: Build generative UI for AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the AG-UI protocol
entry.summary: AWS published a technical guide for building generative UI for AI agents on Bedrock AgentCore using the open AG-UI protocol, which standardizes dynamic agent-to-frontend communication across frameworks. It enables inline charts, shared canvases, and human-in-the-loop approvals.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders Saw This Coming
entry.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders argues that public frustration with Big Tech, billionaires, and unchecked AI is reaching a political tipping point. The interview frames AI concentration of wealth and power as an emerging electoral issue.

entry.title: Lumo, Proton’s privacy-focused AI chatbot, gets an upgrade
entry.summary: Proton's privacy-focused chatbot Lumo received a 2.0 upgrade adding a broader set of capabilities. The update strengthens privacy-oriented alternatives in the assistant space.

entry.title: Featuring Every Eval Ever Results on Hugging Face Model Pages
entry.summary: Hugging Face began featuring Every Eval Ever results directly on model pages, aggregating community evaluations into a central view. It aims to make model comparison more accessible on the platform.

entry.title: Core dump epidemiology: fixing an 18-year-old bug
entry.summary: OpenAI engineers describe using large-scale core dump analysis to debug rare infrastructure crashes, uncovering both a hardware fault and an 18-year-old software bug. The post shares its data-infrastructure debugging approach.

entry.title: How Outpost VFX Uses AWS to Accelerate AI Model Training for Visual Effects
entry.summary: Outpost VFX achieved 8x faster AI model training for face-replacement visual effects using AWS multi-GPU infrastructure. The case study details overcoming single-GPU bottlenecks in production VFX workflows.

entry.title: Simplify multi-account access to Amazon Bedrock models with managed entitlements
entry.summary: AWS described managed entitlements for Amazon Bedrock, letting organizations subscribe to third-party models once from a central account and distribute access across many accounts. It aims to reduce governance overhead for enterprise AI adoption.

entry.title: Implementing resilience patterns with Amazon Bedrock and LLM gateway
entry.summary: AWS outlined resilience patterns for LLM inference using Amazon Bedrock and an LLM gateway, covering model availability, quotas, token limits, and cross-region inference. It targets keeping production generative AI highly available and cost-effective.

entry.title: Building bilingual NER for cargo logistics with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: AWS detailed how IBS Software built a bilingual English-Japanese named-entity-recognition system for cargo logistics using Amazon Bedrock, extracting 23 entity types cost-effectively. It used managed distillation from Amazon Nova Pro for a production-ready solution.

entry.title: Fine-tune Amazon Nova models for accurate email data extraction
entry.summary: AWS described fine-tuning Amazon Nova models to accurately extract structured data from diverse email formats for Parcel Perform, reducing hallucinations and token costs. It addresses common issues like confusing order and tracking numbers in HTML emails.
